paragraphs: Rabbi Padat, son of R’ Eliezer (ben Padat).

Hyman identifies him as a student of his father, citing Berakhot 11b and Moed Katan 20a: R.A. [ר״א] instructed Rabbi Padat, his son. He also transmitted in his father’s name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Yoma, chapter 2, halakhah 3.
And so we find: Rabbi Padat said in the name of Rabbi Yohanan, as in Berakhot 55b; Pesachim 101a; Ketubot 64; Avodah Zarah 38a.
He also spoke in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya, as in Sukkah end of ch. 4; Bava Kamma ch. 4, halakhah 3.

And he was the amora (spokesman) of Rabbi Yasa, as in Megillah ch. 4, end of halakhah 10 [ס״הי]: Rabbi Padat was the amora of Rabbi Yasa. Matters that he had heard from his father he would say as 'Thus said Rabbi in the name of Abba'; matters that he had not heard from his father (and he knew that Rabbi Yasa says it so in the name of his father) he would say 'Thus said Rabbi in the name of Rabbi Elazar.'

And Rabbi Zeira was like his colleague, as in Niddah 8a, where Rabbi Zeira said to him: 'See: between you and your father, you have permitted [it].' Hyman reports that Padat eulogized Rabbi Yohanan, citing Moed Katan 25b (according to the reading of ע״י and דק״ס). His halakhot are mentioned in Shabbat 13a, Eruvin 102a, Yoma 44b and 81b, Chagigah 19a, Bava Batra 171a. Among those who spoke in his name we find R’ Haggai in his name, as in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 24.

Rav Hanan bar Ami said in the name of Rabbi Padat, as in Avodah Zarah 38a. In Pesachim 101a it reads Rabbi Hanin bar Abbaye said in the name of Rabbi Padat; Hyman says it should read Rav Hanan bar Ami, as in Dikdukei Soferim (בדק״ס). In Berakhot 55b it says Rav Huna bar Ami said in the name of Rabbi Padat; Hyman says it appears that it should read Rav Hanan bar Ami.
But where Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin, chapter 10, halakhah 12, has Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi (Ribal) in the name of Rabbi Padat, Hyman says it should read in the name of R’ Padaya.
Rav Yitzhak bar Bisna — he came before Rabbi Padat, as in Yevamot 113b.
Rabbi Yirmeyah in his name, as in Yoma end of ch. 4, ch. 5, halakhah 6.
Hyman reports that when Padat died, R’ Yitzhak bar Bichna eulogized him, citing Moed Katan 25b according to the reading of ע״י and דק״ס.

Evidence correction: the exact retort חזי דמינך ומאבוך קשריתו appears in Niddah_8a.raw.json at he[11] (Sefaria segment 8a:12), immediately after the previously selected Pedat paragraph he[10]. Thus the historical root note reporting bounded nonmatches must not be treated as a current absence conclusion. The raw file was already frozen and remains unchanged. The full named paragraph concerns the combined effect of Pedat’s and his father’s rulings on balsam. This does not settle the separate Moed Katan eulogy variants or harmonize Eliezer in the supplied heading with Elazar elsewhere.

The consulted William Davidson Berakhot 11b and Moed Katan 20a fully name Rabbi Elazar instructing Rabbi Padat, his son. Hyman’s supplied heading instead has Eliezer; R’ Eliezer and his subsequent initials ר״א are retained without silently equating these name forms. The Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud has Padat speaking in Rabbi Lazar’s name at Yoma 2:2, beside Hyman’s supplied 2:3 and his identification of the transmission as being in Padat’s father’s name. Its Hoshaya transmission is at Bava Kamma 4:7, beside Hyman’s 4:3. Hyman’s locators remain in the translation. Sukkah 4:7 supports Rabbi Hoshaya, Megillah 4:10 supports Padat’s role as Rabbi Yasa’s spokesman, and Yoma 4:6 and 5:6 support Yirmeyah’s transmissions. The positive Niddah retort clarifies joint permission, but does not settle either eulogy reading. Hyman’s statements that the names should be changed, including the more qualified “it appears,” remain his judgments. The proposed Padaya and reported Bichna titles remain R’. The siglum ע״י remains unexpanded; Dikdukei Soferim is reported as Hyman cites it, without new apparatus collation. Other unmatched locators, including Yoma 81b and the Haggai reference, remain unverified rather than silently repaired. Both source holds remain in force.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1009) has Eliezer in the heading and uses the initials ר״א in the passage about instructing Padat. The consulted Berakhot 11b and Moed Katan 20a name Rabbi Elazar and call Padat his son. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:10 reports two formulas that Padat used as Rabbi Yasa’s spokesman. The parenthetical explanation of the second formula is Hyman’s.

Hyman reports both that Padat eulogized Rabbi Yohanan and that R’ Yitzhak bar Bichna eulogized Padat. In the consulted Davidson Moed Katan 25b, Rabbi Yitzhak ben Elazar speaks when Rabbi Yohanan dies. In the 1916 Glick Ein Yaakov he delivers the corresponding speech when Rabbi Padat dies. Both accounts then describe Rabbi Ami mourning Rabbi Yohanan. The printed Dikdukei Soferim on 25b (p. 87, note ז) likewise records Padat in its manuscript column where the printed text has Yohanan. That variation identifies the deceased. Hyman’s bar Bichna reading remains uncollated, and the bar Bisna in the consulted Yevamot 113b is recorded separately.
